overview: A solenoid is the simplest possible actuator: a coil of wire around a metal plunger that snaps in (or out, in 'pull' variants) the instant current flows, and springs back the moment it's cut. There's no positioning, no speed control, no direction control — just a fast, forceful on/off motion, which is exactly why they're used for locks, pinball kickers, valves, and vibration/tapping mechanisms. The one spec that catches beginners off guard is duty cycle: many solenoids will overheat and burn out if held energized continuously rather than pulsed, since the coil is only rated for brief activations.
simpleSummary: A coil that snaps a metal rod in or out the instant power is applied — the simplest possible actuator.

specifications.actionType: Push or pull (model-dependent), momentary or latching
specifications.force: Model-dependent, typically a few Newtons for small hobby solenoids
specifications.dutyCycle: Often limited (e.g. 'max 15% duty cycle') — check the datasheet before holding it energized continuously
specifications.current: Can spike well above steady-state draw at the moment of activation

pinMap.name: Coil+
pinMap.function: One coil terminal; energizing the coil actuates the plunger.
pinMap.currentLimit: Model-dependent, often several hundred mA to a few amps
pinMap.gotcha: Most hobby solenoids are not polarity-sensitive (they're just an electromagnet coil), but always check — latching types often are.

pinMap.name: Coil-
pinMap.gotcha: Coils generate a voltage spike when de-energized — a flyback diode across the coil is essential to protect the driving transistor/relay.

useCases.title: Electronic door lock
useCases.scenario: Energize briefly to retract a locking pin, de-energize to let a spring re-lock.

useCases.title: Pinball-style kicker/bumper
useCases.scenario: Fast, forceful momentary push for a game mechanism.

useCases.title: Braille cell / haptic tapper
useCases.scenario: An array of small solenoids providing physical tactile feedback.

oftenConfusedWith: Linear actuators (controllable position/speed, not just snap-action on/off)
oftenUpgradedTo: Linear actuator (when controllable position is needed instead of a snap action)
